_comment: How players come into the world, move between levels and leave it, season to season (crates/bm-world/src/career.rs). classes: kinds of new players, with their age on 1 November of the year they join, the share of pitchers, the level whose talent they start at ('like' a key of levels.json, a level with official statistics) and a shift from it in standard deviations (assumption: about 0.3 SD per year of age between the classes, fitted as a whole with `bm careers`), a factor on the mean growth still ahead of them ('potential', 1 = what aging.json gives for their age), the first-team level whose balance of skills they grow into ('peak'), and the birthplace group. drafts: one national draft per league each autumn, picked in reverse order of the standings; signings: other players each organisation adds every year. positions: primary positions of new position players. retirement: the chance of retiring in the offseason after a season at each age, on top of the players an organisation lets go. keep_potential: how much of the gap between a player's ceiling and his current ability his organisation counts when it decides whom to keep. board_noise: scouting error in the draft order, in standard deviations of ability. Each entry gives its source; 'assumption' marks values without published data. Fitted with CMA-ES (2026-11-16) to each level's attribute means and spreads, ages, the reach rates and each league's rates over a season to 31 May; refitted twice with Levenberg-Marquardt on four seeds: after the league styles, minor-league free agency and the measured age limits (2026-11-16), then after military service and the per-league pitcher shifts and age discounts (2026-11-17), to the leagues' 2025-2026 rates, Baseball-Reference ages and age spreads, the reach rates, the debut age and the majors' power-contact correlation (docs/data-files.md); since then jointly with the markets and the aging (2026-11-19, steps 5-6) and once more in the full recalibration of 2026-11-21 (step 7). Edit freely.

us_college.basis: MLB drafts 2021-2025, 2,277 four-year-college picks (MLB Stats API draft endpoint): 21.95 +- 0.77 years on draft day, 60.6 % pitchers. Starting talent and potential: assumption, fitted with `bm careers`

us_high_school.basis: MLB drafts 2021-2025, 594 high-school picks: 18.51 +- 0.44 years on draft day, 43.9 % pitchers

us_junior_college.basis: MLB drafts 2021-2025, 189 junior-college picks: 20.59 +- 1.06 years, 72 % pitchers

international.basis: Signing rules: 16 before signing, 17 before 1 September of the next year (MLB.com, 2026-01-22). Age spread and share of pitchers: assumption

kbo_high_school.basis: 2027 KBO draft (2026-09-21): 87 of 110 picks high-school seniors, 62 pitchers (isplus, wikitree). Seniors are born in one calendar year, 17.7-18.7 on draft day

kbo_college.basis: 2027 KBO draft: 22 college players (4 early-draft juniors) and one player from abroad

npb_high_school.basis: 2025 NPB draft (2025-10-23): 19 of the 73 main-draft picks from high school, 38 pitchers among the 73 (team lists, spread-sports.jp)

npb_university.basis: 2025 NPB draft: 40 main-draft picks from universities

npb_corporate.basis: 2025 NPB draft: 12 main-draft picks from corporate teams and 2 from independent or other clubs. Ages: assumption (two to six years after high school or university)

npb_development.basis: 2025 NPB development draft: 43 picks, 14 high school, 14 university, 12 independent league, 3 other; 20 pitchers

kr_independent.basis: Assumption: the independent Futures club signs players released by KBO clubs and undrafted amateurs

jp_independent.basis: Assumption: the two independent farm-league clubs sign released NPB players and amateurs

drafts.basis: 20 rounds (615 picks in 2025 with the extra picks); MLB drafts 2021-2025: 74.1 % four-year college (0.4 % other counted with them), 19.3 % high school, 6.2 % junior college; signed 99 % in rounds 1-10 and 85.3 % in rounds 11-20 (a signing bonus recorded)
2026 and 2027 KBO drafts: 11 rounds, 110 picks; 2027: 87 high school, 22 college, 1 from abroad
2025 NPB draft: 73 main-draft picks over 12 clubs (5-7 each; 6 here)

signings.basis: 1,011 international amateurs signed in the 2025 period by 2025-12-02 (Francys Romero, World Baseball Network), about 34 per organisation
2025 NPB development draft: 43 picks over 12 clubs
Assumption: a quarter of a 40-man roster a year
Assumption: a quarter of a 60-man roster a year

positions.basis: Position players in the MLB drafts 2021-2025 (MLB Stats API): OF 12.9 %, SS 7.2 %, C 6.5 %, 1B 4.2 %, 3B 4.1 %, 2B 3.4 %, CF 1.3 %, LF 1.0 %, RF 0.9 %, DH 0.3 % of all picks; the generic OF split evenly over the three outfield positions

starter_share.basis: Share of new amateur pitchers who come in as starters (stamina of a starter). Assumption: most amateur pitchers start; fitted with `bm careers` so that each level keeps the stamina of its pitchers (the share of starters on a roster)

intake_spread.basis: Spread of a new amateur's attributes around his class's means, in standard deviations of the major-league distribution (every level is generated with 1). Assumption, fitted so that each level keeps its spread once growth and the years have spread the players out

intake_tradeoff.basis: Added to the shares of a new amateur's power advantage that come off his contact, timing and bat control (0.80, 0.60, 0.50, measured on major-league regulars: Statcast 2025). Choosing players by value weakens the trade among those who rise, so the amateurs they rise from trade more. Fitted with the majors' power-contact correlation as a target (the first world's -0.694): 0.18 gives -0.654 thirty offseasons on (0: -0.595), at a cost to the leagues' records within the four seeds' noise (decision 2026-11-17)

retirement.basis: Assumption, fitted to the age spread of each level (levels.json): most careers end when no organisation keeps the player; this adds the players who stop on their own

keep_potential.basis: Assumption, fitted to how many draftees of each round reach the majors (Karcher 2017; docs/research/world/aging.md 4B)

board_noise.basis: Scouting error of the draft board, in standard deviations of ability (one board for pitchers and position players). Assumption, fitted to the same reach rates

foreign_candidates.basis: Not used since KBO and NPB clubs sign their foreign players from the world (decision 2026-11-18; contracts.md stage 4): a new player is made only for a slot no player of the world fills

minor_league_contract.basis: Minor-league free agency in a major-league organisation (2023-2027 Minor League Basic Agreement Art. III(A)(1); docs/research/world/contracts_mlb.md 5.8): off the 40-man roster, a player who was 19 or older on the 5 June before he signed his first contract becomes a free agent after parts of six seasons, a younger one after seven. Draftees count their draft year (they sign in July), international amateurs start the season after they sign (15 January). The 40-man roster is taken to be the major-league club and the organisation's next best by the value it keeps players by. With stay_as_depth a free agent re-signs with his organisation, but only for Triple-A or above, the depth veterans sign for (41 % of Triple-A pitchers' playing time goes to pitchers of 28 or older, MLB Stats API 2025-2026); one who does not make it leaves the world, as there is no market yet. Thirty offseasons on, with the same parameters (4 seeds, roster means): Triple-A pitchers 27.4 (Baseball-Reference 27.3; leaving at once gave 24.8, no rule 27.4), Double-A batters 25.6 (23.7; leaving 23.2, no rule 26.8). Remove the entry to turn the rule off (decisions 2026-11-16)

military_service.basis: Korean military service (decisions 2026-11-17; docs/research/world/kbo_notes.md, military service). Every Korean player of a KBO club serves once: by the offseason of the year he turns 27, the age to which Sangmu takes applicants (27 or younger on 31 December, Hankook Ilbo 2018); younger players who are not first-team regulars go earlier, each offseason with early_chance (assumption, fitted to the KBO's ages). Sangmu, the armed forces' team in the Futures League, takes two intakes of 11-15 KBO players a year (15 in the first half of 2024 and of 2025, 11 in the second half of 2026): the best 26 who may still apply, the others serve on active duty and do not play (they age, but do not grow). The service lasts about 18 months: half the players are away one season, half two (the May intake misses half a season and the next, the December intake the next season and half the one after). Players in service do not count against the 68-player limit (KBO bylaw article 24). Exempt: the Asian Games team after a gold (sports service: four weeks of basic training; Olympic medals as well, not modelled), every four years from 2030: 24 players, 11 of them pitchers, 25 or younger bar three wildcards, at most three from one club (2026 Aichi-Nagoya rules); gold in 7 of Korea's 9 Asian Games, five in a row from 2010; the history of a new world has them as well, in step with 2030 (2010, 2014, 2018, 2022, 2026; the 2022 Games were held in 2023)

history.basis: Offseasons without games a new world goes through before its first season (decision 2026-11-18: start from a settled world): the first world is made that many years before the start (2007 for a 2027 start) and the game begins with what the career model makes of it. From the first world itself the major-league first teams' hitters rose from +7 runs per 162 games above their target of -1.0 (offseason 1) to +28 (offseason 7) and settled near +9 from offseason 20 on, and the majors' free-agent market fell from about 177 major-league signings a year to 48-62 (offseasons 6-11) before it came back to 166-178 (offseasons 20-30; seeds 5-8). (these counts are from before the joint careers and market fit of 2026-11-19). The careers were fitted on offseasons 16-30

age_discount.basis: Standard deviations of ability taken off a player's worth for each year of age past 30 when his organisation decides whom to keep: older players cost more (no salaries are modelled yet) and have less ahead of them. Assumption, fitted with `bm careers` to the ages of each level

league_age_discount.basis: Added to age_discount by the organisations of each league (decision 2026-11-17). KBO clubs keep their veterans far longer than the majors' organisations: Baseball-Reference 2025-2026 gives KBO batters an age spread of 5.45 years and 43.5 % of their playing time at 30 or older (NPB 3.95 years, MLB 3.67), which one discount for every league could not keep. Fitted with the leagues' ages and records

pitcher_potential.basis: Factor on the growth ahead of new pitchers against new position players. Assumption, fitted with `bm careers`

pitcher_shift.basis: Standard deviations added to new pitchers' pitching on top of their class's talent: how far behind the position players of their age they start. Assumption, fitted with `bm careers` to the ages of each level

league_pitcher_shift.basis: Standard deviations added to pitcher_shift for the new pitchers of each kind of league. Introduced when the NPB farm's pitchers sat 1.17 SD below the first team's (the levels of 2026-11-17) where its hitters sat 0.57 below, and thirty offseasons on the first team's pitchers came out 0.7-1.0 SD weaker than its records asked (decision 2026-11-17). Fitted with the leagues' records, last with the careers and markets together (2026-11-19)

prospect_spread.basis: Standard deviation of the logarithm of a player's personal growth factor (median 1). Assumption, fitted with `bm careers` to the reach rates by draft round and to each level's talent

balance.basis: Share of a level's skill gaps (more raw power than bat-to-ball skill, weaker defence and bodies, poor command, nearly major-league velocity, plate discipline as good as the majors) that closes by a player's peak. Assumption, fitted with `bm careers` so that each level keeps the skill balance of its 2025-2026 statistics

styles.basis: Shifts of the new amateurs each kind of league takes in (mlb: the major-league organisations, kbo, npb), in standard deviations, applied to their attributes before their ceilings are drawn, so that both move: hitters' power, bat-to-ball skills (contact, timing, bat control) and plate discipline, pitchers' stuff (stuff, deception, pitch grades). The amateur game and the clubs of each league shape this mix; choosing players by value alone gathers power and discipline at the top of every league. Shifting the ceilings alone moved nothing where a ceiling lies below the player (the NPB's power, the majors' plate discipline: +0.4 moved them +0.004 and +0.037 after 30 offseasons; decision 2026-11-16). The first world's players already have their league's balance and are not shifted. Fitted so that the world after 30 offseasons plays each league's 2025-2026 records
